glosses: A long-drawn, high-pitched complaining cry or sound.

examples.text: The 18-year-old [Justin] Bieber can’t quite pull off the “adult” thing just yet: His voice may have dropped a bit since the days of “Baby,” but it still mostly registers as “angelic,” and veers toward a pubescent whine at times.

glosses: A complaint or criticism.

examples.text: I need to have a quick whine about my boss before we start talking about the holiday.
Eighner, in particular, is infamous for his "what publishers and editors did to poor me" whines.

glosses: To utter a high-pitched cry.
To make a sound resembling such a cry.

examples.text: The jet engines whined at take off.

glosses: To complain or protest with a whine (compare whinge) or as if with a whine.

examples.text: [S]he was one of your ſoft ſpoken, canting, whining hypocrites, who with a truly jeſuitical art, could wreſt evil out of the moſt inoffenſive thought, word, look or action; […]
Feel awfully about Scott... I always knew he couldn't think—he never could—but he had a marvelous talent and the thing is to use it—not whine in public.

glosses: To move with a whining sound.

examples.text: The jet whined into the air.
The wind whined and moaned through the trees.

glosses: To utter with the sound of a whine.

examples.text: The child whined all his complaints.
Kelly Queen was whining that the boss made him put on his tie.

glosses: To repeatedly remind or complain to (someone) in an annoying way, often about insignificant or unnecessary matters.

examples.text: The room is never cleaned, so her mother nags and nags until she explodes with frustration and threatens to sell her to the lowest bidder.

glosses: To bother with persistent thoughts or memories.

examples.text: The notion that he forgot something nagged him the rest of the day.

You are sleeping on your side in the bed in your flat, heavily embroiled in a dream which sucks and nags at you and makes no sense; an old primary school teacher is there and a cat you have to take to a supermarket; you are in a canoe.

glosses: To bother or disturb persistently in any way.

examples.text: But at night, around the uncertain edge of dreams, and when the wind nags, there are few whom an odd sound will not thrill

glosses: Someone or something that nags.

examples.text: And finally the biggest thank you of all to my partner Steven Winston for your love, enthusiasm, encouragement, support, humour, nags, and glasses of wine.

glosses: A persistent, bothersome thought or worry.

examples.text: All that while there was a little nag going on at the back of his mind, which he strove to disregard. But it insisted on attention, and to get rid of it he put down his palette abruptly and got out his mustard-tin cash-box and counted his money.
